newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit reverses early trend, ends slightly up - Sep 5.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit reverses early trend, ends slightly up - Sep 5.

text.p: The ringgit closed slightly higher against the dollar, reversing its early trend due to some strong offshore bids for the local currency and profit-taking on the dollar, dealers said.
But trading was thin throughout the day as the market stayed focused on Friday's U.S. employment data.

"Nobody seems to be taking large positions though I believe the U.S. jobs data will not have much impact on the market," said one dealer with a foreign bank. "But there's nothing else to trade on at the moment."
Dealers said muted dollar/majors movements also kept dollar/ringgit in a tight range through the session.
The ringgit had earlier extended its softer undertone following commercial sales by a bank in Singapore.
At the local 1000 GMT close, the ringgit was at 2.4962/72 per dollar against 2.4967/72 on Wednesday.
On the money market, interbank rates stayed firm on tighter supply of short-term funds and borrowings by finance houses and small commercial banks, dealers said.
The overnight rate closed at 8.50 percent, unchanged from Wednesday, after trading between 8.20 and 8.60 percent.
